Guidance & outlook: The dip, which is visible in the third quarter of FY26, was on account of reversal of an other income item, which we had booked in the second quarter of FY26.
We expect the cash position to improve going forward.

And we've guided earlier that you should target a blended EBITDA of 3 5%, I think you will be able to make a fairly accurate assessment of the way the revenue will shape up in the second half of the current financial year.
Growth & demand: In the presentation, we've put out the order book and bifurcated it rig -wise and day rate-wise so that one is able to assess how the revenue will shape up going forward.
The order book stands at INR1,310 crores, and we've also bifurcated the order book year-wise.

The rate is something on which I cannot comment because if you look at our order book on Slide 5, you will see the massive fluctuation in the day rates despite these rigs getting redeployed in a similar time period.
Margins & costs: The variation in EBITDA is primarily on account of the variation in other expenses, which is caused by forex fluctuation, which was more prevalent in the last quarter of the previous financial year and less prevalent in the first quarter of the current financial year.
EBITDA mix is given on the subsequent slide with most of the EBITDA coming from the rig segment.
Considering the recent inflationary trend and the increase in labor cost and transit cost of materials, I think a figure between INR90 crores to INR110 crores would be a fair estimate per rig.
Capex & expansion: We remain a cash -rich organization des pite having acquired one rig in FY25 and conducting refurbishment exercise of the said rig.
As of now, we are not looking at any acquisitions right now.
Balance sheet & cash: Question two is, I think our cash position has improved meaningfully and also, I believe the debt has gone down, which obviously allows us the flexibility to kind of raise more funds.
There is a receivable of INR63 crores, the original receivable of INR63 crores.
Risks & challenges: Despite that challenge, we remain fairly confident that we'll be able to redeploy these three rigs.

However, I do not believe that EBITDA will decline in proportion to the decline in revenue because right now, we are earning most of our EBITDA from the rigs which we own or from the rigs that are deployed at a good rate.
So although there will be a Jindal Drilling & Industries Limited August 10, 2026 decline in revenue from 3 rigs, the decline in earnings would primarily be from 2 rigs.

Guidance & outlook: We are concluding one today, and they are expected to come out with another tender very soon for 4 rigs.
And in the coming few weeks or months, we expect a few more tenders coming out from ONGC, where we will bid the other rigs that will be dehiring this year.
And next year also, I think we will do around INR350 crores of EBITDA.
Growth & demand: And globally, the demand of rigs are also going up since Saudi Aramco has taken back its rigs.
When we look in your presentation, Kaushal ji, you have mentioned order book for Q4.
But nothing in the pipeline for this year as such.
Margins & costs: We will be doing INR350 crores of EBITDA in the current year, slightly more than that.
And for them to change it to an ONGC requirement would be a very high cost, and that cost would not be equivalent to the rates that you get in India.
On Slide number 8, the total revenue is shown EBIT and EBITDA margin is shown.
Capex & expansion: So, I was going for like some other country, for the companies as well , there is something cal led tonnage tax where the government pushes the company to pay tax less and reserve that money to acquire more vessels.
In addition to that, there is also dues to the vendor from whom we have acquired Jindal Pioneer.

But -- so next year, the upside would come from the rig that will get deployed now one, yes, it is not in the current and the volatile part would be -- it goes higher or lower, perhaps lower from the rigs that get decommissioned in 2026 or whenever there was 3 rigs, yes.
Balance sheet & cash: In the previous call, we had highlighted that there was an old litigation with ONGC, which had favourably concluded and we had made a gain of around INR100 crores on the original receivable of INR66 crores.
Therefore, we have doubled the dividend which was paid out in the previous financial year from the level it was in the year before that.
Risks & challenges: But the rates in India were affected due to competition in the last tender.
So, we don't see much international competition entering the market for ONGC.
I can't really talk about the competition as to what they will be doing.
